target.title: fix(ui): avoid fallback main session parent in Control UI
target.body:
Closes #93422

## Summary

- **Fix classification:** root-cause user-facing Control UI session naming bug fix; this fixes the command-to-session-label routing invariant instead of adding a second naming field.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** high for the technical label-contract fix; the remaining `/new <text>` command grammar is a maintainer UX decision and is documented below.
- **Root cause:** Control UI handled typed chat commands locally, but `/new <name>` did not carry the typed name through the real `ChatPage` session-creation adapter, and `/label <name>` was not registered as a local Control UI command. Earlier iterations also tried a separate writable `displayName` path, which conflicted with the existing session `label` contract.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the typed Control UI command now routes the requested visible name through the existing gateway `label` source of truth for both `sessions.create` and `sessions.patch`, including the `session.dmScope: "main"` reset-in-place path. This avoids adding a second writable naming field.
- **Patch quality notes:** this stays on the existing `label` contract, documents the Control UI-specific command semantics, and keeps generated protocol/create/patch surfaces free of writable `displayName` inputs. The broad `catch` in `/label` is the local command error-surface used to show gateway patch failures in the chat input. The `as unknown` casts are contained to tests that construct a minimal `ApplicationContext`/browser client fixture for the real `ChatPage` adapter.

## Linked context

- **Issue:** Closes #93422.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** users can type `/new Research Plan` in Control UI to create a named chat and `/label Work Plan` to rename the current chat, and the label persists through the gateway session store and session list.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** session naming is written through the existing `label` field on `sessions.create` and `sessions.patch`, which is the existing gateway source of truth for persisted session labels. The PR deliberately does not add `displayName` to gateway protocol create/patch schemas, Swift generated create/patch models, or the Control UI write path, so compatibility risk stays limited to command semantics rather than a new wire/data contract.
- **Related open PR / same-contract scan:** related session-label work exists, including the merged `/name <title>` command path and broader named-new command work, but those do not replace the Control UI typed `/new <name>` path fixed here. This PR follows the accepted `label` direction instead of introducing a parallel naming contract.
- **What did NOT change:** no model routing, auth, archive/pin semantics, transcript format, permissions, dependencies, workflows, generated protocol create/patch writable `displayName` surface, or cross-channel command behavior changed. Non-Control-UI command semantics remain outside this PR.
- **Out of scope:** cross-channel command grammar, a visual session-picker recording, and broader session-label UX consolidation remain maintainer/product follow-ups.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Control UI `/new <name>` creates a session with that visible label, Control UI `/label <name>` patches the active session label, and the main-session reset-in-place path preserves the requested label when applicable.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** local gateway RPC proof exercised `sessions.create` with `label: "Research Plan"`, `sessions.list` filtering by that label, `sessions.patch` to change the label to `"Work Plan"`, and a store read confirming the patched label persisted.
- **Evidence after fix:** focused gateway, Control UI, protocol/command, and Swift-generation validations passed after the label-contract change.
- **Observed result after fix:** the created session was returned and listed by `Research Plan`; the patched session was returned and listed by `Work Plan`; the store persisted the patched `label`; typed `/new <name>` and `/label <name>` are covered by focused UI tests.
- **What was not tested:** no browser screencast or Mantis visual recording is attached. ClawSweeper marked the local gateway RPC proof and focused validations as sufficient, while noting that a visual Control UI recording would still help review.

## Tests and validation

- Focused gateway validation passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` — 5 files passed, 207 tests passed.
- Focused Control UI validation passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-page.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-state.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-commands.test.ts` — 4 files passed, 115 tests passed.
- Protocol and command validation passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/auto-reply/commands-registry.test.ts src/commands/sessions.test.ts` — 3 files passed, 96 tests passed.
- Swift protocol generation was rerun and verified idempotent after the schema check.
- **Target test file:** `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts` covers typed `/new <name>` and `/label <name>` command dispatch; `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-page.test.ts` covers the real `ChatPage` adapter forwarding `label`; gateway tests cover label persistence and reset-in-place behavior.
- **Scenario locked in:** typed Control UI session naming must use `label`, not a parallel writable `displayName`, and fallback/synthetic parent rows must not be used as new-chat parents.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** the tests cover the actual command dispatch, real page adapter boundary, gateway create/patch persistence, and reset-in-place edge case without adding unrelated command or protocol behavior.

## Risk checklist

- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility and session-state.
- **Risk explanation:** compatibility risk comes from documenting that Control UI treats bare `/new <text>` as a label shortcut even though shared command docs also describe model-oriented `/new [model]` behavior. Session-state risk comes from writing persistent labels and guarding new-chat parent selection.
- **Why acceptable:** the behavior is limited to typed Control UI local handling, the docs now call out the Control UI-specific semantics and direct model changes to `/model`, and the persistence path uses the existing `label` contract with regression coverage. The remaining command-grammar choice is visible for maintainer review rather than hidden in code.

## Current review state

- **RF-001 — ClawSweeper P1 `/new <text>` docs/UX split:** addressed as documentation alignment plus maintainer decision. `docs/tools/slash-commands.md` now states that Control UI uses text after `/new` as a session label and points model changes to `/model`. The UX choice remains explicitly called out in this PR body.
- **RF-002 — ClawSweeper P1 persistent labels/session-state contract:** addressed for the technical contract. The code writes through existing `label` create/patch semantics, avoids a new writable `displayName` contract, and records the session-state risk above for maintainer review.
- **RF-003 — ClawSweeper P2 maintainer UX approval/documentation alignment:** addressed by adding the docs alignment and preserving the maintainer decision note in this section.
- **RF-004 — ClawSweeper P3 document Control UI naming commands:** fixed by documenting Control UI `/new <text>` and `/label <name>` behavior in the slash-command docs.
